chunks: What the Shaykh, may Allah support him, informed me of: from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from his father, from Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā and al-Ḥusayn ibn ʿUbayd Allāh, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from his father Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī ibn Maḥbūb, from al-ʿAbbās, from al-Ḥasan ibn Maḥbūb, from ʿAlī ibn Riʾāb, from Ibrāhīm ibn Maymūn, who said:
I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about a man whose garment falls upon the body of the dead person.

He عليه السلام said: "If the dead person has been given ghusl, then do not wash what of it has touched your garment; but if the dead person has not been given ghusl, then wash what of it has touched your garment."

Then he said, may Allah the Exalted support him: if it falls upon a carcass other than that of humans, it also renders it impure, and it becomes obligatory upon him to wash it from that with water. The principle in this is that the dead body is impure without disagreement, and when impurity comes into contact with the garment, it is obligatory to purify it so that one may be certain of entering the salat with the garment in a state of taharah; and this is also indicated by other evidence.

key_terms.الْمَيِّتِ: the dead person whose body is being discussed in the ruling
key_terms.ثَوْبَكَ: your garment, the item potentially affected by najasah
key_terms.غَسْلُهُ: washing it with water to remove impurity
key_terms.غُسِّلَ: was given ghusl, the ritual washing of the deceased
key_terms.مَيْتَةٍ: a carcass, especially a dead animal not lawfully purified

ai.seo_question: Does a garment become najis if it touches a dead body before or after the deceased is washed?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about contact between a garment and a dead body. It states that if the deceased has already been given ghusl, the affected part of the garment does not need washing, but if the deceased has not been washed, the garment must be washed. The accompanying juristic note generalizes the principle of impurity from contact with a carcass and emphasizes taharah of clothing for salat.
